metadata.title: Temperature development in a massive concrete cube (COST TU1404 Task 2 - Azenha et al.)
metadata.validation_method: Comparison with experimental temperature histories at 3 thermocouples (core TP18, surface TP9 mid-height 5cm from side, TP3 5cm from side and 5cm from bottom) from Azenha et al. 2011, digitized from Fig.7 / Fig.18-19 of benchmark paper
metadata.validation_target: Core (TP18) peak 55.1 C at 7.2 h and 27.6 C at 24 h; TP9 peak ~50.5 C, TP3 peak ~47 C (Fig.7/18/19). Teams 1,2,3,7 land within 0.2-2.5 C, which the paper states is the measurement precision.
metadata.notes: 2D cross-section 0.4m cube. Hydration Team2 OOFEM Table13. Bottom 5.208 W/m2K, lateral 5.208->10 at 8.6h, top 10. Reference CSVs now from user-extracted Fig7 (TP18,TP9,TP3) data (19).csv and Fig18 core measured data (20).csv. Converted from time_d [days] to time_h [hours] (time_h=time_d*24). Headers cleaned to time_h,T_degC matching x_col/y_col. CORRECTED 2026-08-22: all convection coefficients scaled by 1.5 to compensate the missing third dimension (see boundary_conditions _comment_alpha); TP18_core.csv digitized from Fig.7; the dangling TP18_measured_fig18 reference was replaced by the team-envelope plot.
metadata._comment_dimension: PAPER_VALUE: 2D model used by several teams (Fig.14-15), quarter symmetry optional. Full 0.4x0.4 square chosen for simplicity, dimension must match mesh (2).

points.name: TP3_bottom
points._comment: PAPER_VALUE: TP3 - 5 cm beneath lateral surface and 5 cm from lower face (Fig.6). x=0.35, y=0.05

mesh._comment_element_size: INFERRED: 20 mm gives 20 elements per side, sufficient to resolve thermal gradient. 400mm/10 =40mm max for bending, but thermal needs finer. Teams used 5mm (Fig.15) - we use 20mm for speed, refinement possible via CLI preset.

geometry._comment_dimension_correction: NB the _comment_dimension above is wrong: Fig.14 is a 3D model (Teams 1,2,3,7); only Team 4's Fig.15 is 2D. This file stays 2D and corrects for it through the convection coefficients.

heat_transport._comment: PAPER_VALUE: thermal field, Eq (1) k div grad T + Qdot = rho c Tdot

hydration._comment: PAPER_VALUE: hydration degree drives heat release, affinity model Eq (3)

temperature._comment_k: PAPER_VALUE: Table 5 thermal conductivity 2.6 W/(K m) (written as W/(K m3) but meaning W/mK)
temperature._comment_rho: INFERRED: sum of mix components Table 4: 430+301.5+339.7+335+729.7+193.4+6.8 = 2336.1 kg/m3, rounded 2335.1. Density not given directly, inferred from mix.
temperature._comment_cp: INFERRED: volumetric heat capacity 2400 kJ/(K m3) =2.4e6 J/K/m3 Table 5 divided by rho 2335 => 1028 J/kgK. Product rho*cp =2.4e6 matches Table 5.
temperature._comment_sanity: Sanity Check 2 & 3: dT_ad = Hu*c_cement*alpha_inf/(rho*cp) = 500e3*430*0.875/2.4e6=78.4K. Measured rise ~22K (26->48 core), so dT_ad > measured, BCs must carry off ~56K - passes. Cooling tau = rho cp V/(h A) =2.4e6*0.064/(10*0.96)=16000s~4.4h matches observed cooling over 24h.

degree_of_hydration._comment_B1: PAPER_VALUE: Team 2 (OOFEM) Table 13 B1=0.0002916 1/s, affinity law after [14]
degree_of_hydration._comment_alpha_inf: PAPER_VALUE: Team 2 Table 13 amax=0.875 ultimate hydration degree
degree_of_hydration._comment_eta: PAPER_VALUE: Team 2 Table 13 g=5.554 microdiffusion parameter, maps to eta in OOFEM
degree_of_hydration._comment_Ea: INFERRED: Ea/R=5653 1/K Table 13 Team 2, *R 8.314 =46999 J/mol. PAPER_VALUE Ea/R, INFERRED Ea.
degree_of_hydration._comment_T_ref: PAPER_VALUE: affinity ~A25 at 25C, so T_ref=25C=298.15K KELVIN - only Kelvin temp in file
degree_of_hydration._comment_Hu: PAPER_VALUE: Team 2 Table 13 Qpot=500 J/g total hydration heat for complete hydration
degree_of_hydration._comment_c_cement: PAPER_VALUE: Table 4 cement content 430 kg/m3 CEM I 52.5R
degree_of_hydration._comment_B1_unit: PAPER_VALUE: B1 already in 1/s, no conversion
degree_of_hydration._comment_sanity_Hu: PAPER_VALUE: Qpot 500 J/g matches CEM I typical 400-500 J/g literature

initial_conditions._comment: PAPER_VALUE: Table 5 concrete initial temperature 26 C, DEGREES CELSIUS

boundary_conditions._comment_alpha: 2D->3D CORRECTION (factor 1.5): the benchmark specimen is a 400 mm CUBE cooled on 6 faces (A/V = 6/L = 15 1/m); this 2D cross-section is cooled on 4 edges only (A/V = 4/L = 10 1/m), so it loses heat 1/3 too slowly. Verified: uncorrected 2D gives core peak 64.0 C @ 9.8 h and T(24h)=36.0 C against a measured 55.1 C @ 7.2 h and 27.6 C; an independent 3D FD run with these exact parameters gives 57.0/27.5 and the h*1.5 2D run gives 57.4/29.5. Teams 1,2,3,7 modelled this in 3D (Fig.14); only Team 4 used 2D (Fig.15) and deviates. Raw h from Table 5 is quoted in _comment_alpha_paper below.
boundary_conditions._comment_u_ref: PAPER_VALUE: Table 5 climatic chamber 20 C, DEGREES CELSIUS

reference_curves.label: TP18 core measured Fig.7 (digitized)
reference_curves._comment: PAPER_VALUE: digitized from Fig.7 by colour extraction of the red TP18 series at 300 dpi (axes calibrated on the 0/1 d ticks and the 20..60 C gridlines). Peak 55.1 C at 7.21 h, T(24h)=27.6 C. The record starts at 3.6 h -- Fig.7 has no continuous data before that, only an isolated t~0 cluster at 24-28 C -- so the curve legitimately begins mid-plot.
